questions.question: Write the functions of source, monnochromator and detector.
questions.solution_html:
• Source: Provides stable, intense radiation across desired wavelengths (e.g.
  • deuterium lamp for UV, Nernst glower for IR).
  • Monochromator: Disperses polychromatic light into individual wavelengths using
  • grating/prism.
  • Detector: Converts light signal into electrical output proportional to intensity
  • (photodiode, PMT).
  • → Together they enable accurate measurement of absorbance and transmittance.
  • ((1 mark) each = 3)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the working principle of Tandem Mass Spectrometry (MS/MS) and its analytical applications.
questions.solution_html:
• Tandem MS involves two mass analyzers separated by a collision cell. The first MS
  • selects a specific parent ion. Collision-induced dissociation breaks it into fragment
  • ions. The second MS analyzes these fragments to identify structure.
  • 25900407
  • Applications include drug profiling, protein sequencing, and toxicological screening.
  • (Principle–2 ; Applications–1)

questions.question: What is the basic principle of GC-MS?
questions.solution_html:
• Gas chromatography first separates volatile compounds based on partition between
  • stationary and mobile phases. The effluent enters the mass spectrometer where
  • molecules are ionized and sorted by mass-to-charge ratio. The combination provides
  • both qualitative and quantitative identification. (Separation–1 ; Ionization–1 ;
  • Identification–1)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the role of a detector in IR spectroscopy?
questions.solution_html:
• The detector converts transmitted IR radiation into an electrical signal.
  • Common detectors include Thermocouple, Golay cell, and DTGS.
  • They measure intensity differences between sample and reference beams, producing
  • absorbance spectra for functional group identification.
  • (Working–2 ; Example–1)

questions.question: Determine the principle of Mass Spectrometry (MS).
questions.solution_html:
• Mass spectrometry measures mass-to-charge ratio of ions.
  • Sample molecules are ionized (electron impact or ESI), accelerated by electric fields
  • and separated in mass analyzers (quadrupole, TOF).
  • Detector records intensity to produce a mass spectrum used for identification and
  • quantification.
  • (Ionization–1 ; Separation–1 ; Detection–1)
  • Short Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the contribution of detectors in improving chromatographic analysis in forensic investigations.
questions.solution_html:
• Detectors transform the separated components into measurable signals, increasing
  • sensitivity and precision. Types and contributions: UV–Vis Detector: Measures
  • absorbance of eluted species. Fluorescence Detector: Enhances selectivity for
  • fluorescent compounds. Refractive Index Detector: Universal but less sensitive.
  • Electron Capture Detector (GC): Highly sensitive for halogenated compounds. Mass
  • spectrometric Detector: Provides molecular identity and quantitation. Detectors allow
  • trace-level analysis in forensic samples like drugs, inks, and toxicants. (Definition–1;
  • Types–3; Forensic importance–2)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the width of absorption lines and their role in interpretation of NMR?
questions.solution_html:
• Line width depends on magnetic field homogeneity and relaxation time (T ). Broader
  • lines: short relaxation, less resolution. Narrow lines: better separation of chemical
  • shifts and coupling. Inter-nuclear interactions and viscosity also affect width.
  • Understanding line width aids in accurate chemical shift and multiplet analysis for
  • structural elucidation. (Definition–2; Factors–2; Importance–2)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss energy transitions in UV - visible spectroscopy.
questions.solution_html:
• Electronic transitions occur when molecules absorb UV–Vis radiation (200–800 nm).
  • Types: σ→σ*, n→σ*, π→π*, n→π*.
  • Transition energy depends on bond type and substituents.
  • Chromophores and auxochromes shift absorption bands (hypsochromic or
  • bathochromic shifts).
  • Used to identify conjugation and concentration via Beer–Lambert Law.
  • (Transitions–3; Influence–2; Application–1)

questions.question: Explain the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter in detail with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Electromagnetic radiation interacts with matter through absorption, emission
  • reflection, or scattering.
  • Different frequencies produce distinct phenomena.
  • Region Type of Interaction Effect
  • Gamma X-ray Ionization Ejection of electrons
  • UV–Visible Electronic excitation n→π*, π→π* transitions
  • IR Vibrational Bond stretch and bend
  • Microwave Rotational Molecular rotation
  • Radio Nuclear spin transitions Basis of NMR
  • Marking (15): Concept–3; Table–5; Beer–Lambert–2; Selection rules–2;
  • Applications–2; Conclusion–1.

questions.question: Define Scanning modes SIM & Full SCAN
questions.solution_html:
• In mass spectrometry, scanning modes determine how the instrument collects ion
  • signals to analyze a sample. The two commonly used modes are Full Scan and SIM
  • (Selected Ion Monitoring).
  • Feature Full Scan SIM
  • m/z Range Broad (50–500) Few specific m/z values
  • 25900407
  • Purpose Qualitative analysis Quantitative analysis
  • Sensitivity Lower Higher
  • Use Case Screening unknowns Targeted compound detection
  • Definition of both modes – (4 marks), Principles and working – (4 marks)
  • Advantages/Limitations – (4 marks), Forensic application and conclusion – (3 marks)
